description: Two or more tool calls in a row folded into one quiet line, "› 5 tool calls", with a spinner after it while one runs. Opened, the calls are listed under it, a ToolCall card each, their boxes starting where the chat's text starts (no indent).
opens: A second tool call arriving right after another (nothing but tool calls between them)

parts.name: line
parts.shows: A 16px disclosure arrow (› pointing right when folded, ⌄ down when open, at 75% opacity) then the label at 80% opacity: "N tool calls", with ", F failed" when any failed and ", I interrupted" when any were interrupted (e.g. "6 tool calls, 1 failed"). 2px above and below. Then, while any call in it runs (or runs in the background), a 16px spinner; nothing when all are done (a tick wouldn't say anything).

actions.does: Slides the list of calls open (120ms) or closed. The line stays put on screen; what's under it moves. Pointer: a hand.

parts.name: calls
parts.shows: Opened: each call's card (ToolCall), one under another 4px apart, 4px under the line, full width, left edge where the chat's text starts. Each card is a single line until its own toggles are opened.

states.name: folded
states.shows: Just the line. This is how a finished run of calls normally sits in the chat.

states.name: running
states.shows: Spinner after the label. A call waiting for your permission doesn't count as running.

states.name: opens by itself
states.shows: When any call in it has images to show, or is asking for permission, the group opens so you see it.

states.name: how runs form
states.shows: Only consecutive tool calls group; Claude's text or thinking between calls ends the run (the next calls start a new group, or stay a lone card). A lone call is a bare card, not a group. Mesh calls (MeshCard) never join a group and split a run.
